  "counter_arguments": "BOUNDARY DISPUTES:

1. Lafayette/James Madison/Benjamin Franklin grouping: Sources disagree whether these are one class (31 boats) or three classes. Wikipedia notes 'combined in some references.' Default decision: treat as three separate classes with distinct hull number blocks, but acknowledge the grouping exists.

2. Gar class vs Tambor subclass: Some sources treat Gar as subclass of Tambor, others as separate. Included separately as they have distinct hull numbers and represent incremental improvement.

3. GUPPY conversions: Not included as separate class because GUPPY was modernization program applied to existing Gato/Balao/Tench boats that retained original class designations.

4. Research submarines (NR-1, Dolphin): Excluded as non-combat specialized vessels. Albacore included because it directly influenced combat submarine design.

5. Unique boats as 'classes': USS Nautilus, Seawolf, Triton, Tullibee, Narwhal, Glenard P. Lipscomb, Albacore, Darter, X-1, M-1 all included as they represent distinct commissioned designs even though single boats.

6. Ohio SSGN conversions: Treated as single Ohio class with conversion noted, not separate class, consistent with Halibut SSGN-to-SSN treatment.

7. Migraine class: Mentioned in navigation lists but unverified, excluded pending confirmation.

8. Exact counts for Porpoise/Salmon/Sargo: Classes confirmed but exact numbers not fully verified in search results, approximate counts provided.",
